title: Finding the Largest / Smallest
objectives: Find the largest (or smallest) value in an array with a scan that makes comparisons

hook.text: You want to find the highest grade in a class. You do not even need to sort the array. A smart scan is enough.

concept.heading: A scan with comparisons
concept.body: To find the largest value: first take the FIRST element of the array as the "current largest". Then compare the other elements with it one by one; if you find a larger element, update the "current largest". When the array ends, the value you are holding is the true largest.

concept.heading: Why start from the first element?
concept.body: Starting with "largest ← 0" is dangerous: what if ALL the numbers in the array are negative? Then 0 is never updated and gives a wrong result. That is why you always start from a REAL element of the array (the first element).

workedExamples.prompt: Find the largest number in an array.
workedExamples.runnerSource:
numbers ← [12, 45, 7, 32]
largest ← numbers[0]
FOR i ← 1 TO 3 STEP 1
  IF numbers[i] > largest
    largest ← numbers[i]
  END
END_LOOP
WRITE largest

steps.explain: largest starts with the first element (12).
i = 2: 7 > 45 is FALSE, so nothing changes. i = 3: 32 > 45 is FALSE, so nothing changes.

exercises.question: What does this code write to the screen?
Why is the largest variable started with "numbers[0]" instead of "0"?
options: If all the numbers in the array are negative, 0 is never updated and gives a wrong result

feedback.correct: Correct. Starting from a real element of the array also guarantees the right result when all numbers are negative.
feedback.incorrect: If all the numbers are negative, starting from 0 leads to a wrong result that is never updated.

exercises.question: Put the steps of the algorithm that finds the largest element in the correct order.
steps: largest ← the first element of the array
Walk through the array starting from the second element
If it is larger, update largest

exercises.question: When searching for the largest element, why does the loop start from the SECOND element (index 1) of the array?
options: The first element is already taken as the "current largest", so there is no need to check it again
The first element is always wrong
The first element can never be the largest

feedback.correct: Correct. Since the first element is already the starting value, the remaining elements (from index 1) are scanned.
feedback.incorrect: The first element is already the starting value of largest, so the loop starts from the second element.

exercises.hint: largest changes only when a larger element is found.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.template: When searching for the largest element, the ___ element of the array is used as the starting value.

summary: Finding the largest/smallest: start from the first element of the array and move on by comparing with the others.
The starting value is a real element of the array (the first element), not 0.
The loop can start from the second element (index 1) because the first element is already the starting value.
